# Mathematical notes on scans 573–587

The scans start in a proof and end with working outlines. Section and lemma numbers below are the author’s. The notes follow the frozen reading. M1 and M2 identify checks recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

## What the pages do

**573–574 · End of the transfinite construction.** The initial paragraph excludes a small subfamily of the closed subcategories generated by individual objects. For the converse the author well-orders the objects of an underlined S and recursively chooses objects xα, avoiding the closed subcategory generated by the previous choices. The displayed vanishing of Hom, the comparison with sα and the two inclusions on 574 are the recorded conclusions.

**574–575 · Proposition 4.16.7.5.** For a given universe the author compares the existence of a nonaccessible closed subcategory with that of a transfinite family in a category written C with a hat. Its forward Hom sets are empty for α<β. He takes M to be the hatted category for one implication and embeds M in such a category for the other. The arguments of Hom in the definition are transcribed exactly as written.

**575–576 · Existence and examples.** The next paragraph records a failed attempt to construct the family or exclude it, followed by the special case of a transfinite sequence of fields. The question broadens to L-stable subcategories. The author recalls an open-subcategory example from an appendix. His two later marginal responses accompany the earlier writing.

**577 · Proposition 4.16.7.6.** For an open subcategory S of an accessible M he states an accessibility criterion in terms of L-stability and a cardinal π₀. At a suitable π≥π₀ the conclusion is π-accessibility. An insertion restates the condition for a cardinal useful for M.

**577 · Corollary 4.16.7.7.** The object x is presented as a direct limit of xᵢ, with a separate condition on I. The last display tests membership in S by membership of all the xᵢ in the indicated intersection S(π). A marginal instruction groups this statement with its proposition and points ahead to 4.16.7.8.

**578 · Proposition 4.16.7.8.** Four conditions concern S, the open complementary T, and a fixed infinite useful cardinal π. They compare π-accessibility of S, generation from S(π), π-accessibility of T, and Lπ-stability of T. The generation condition is also written using an existential ξ and a nonempty Hom. The word “fermée” in the initial description of S is crossed.

**578–579 · Corollary 4.16.7.9.** The version without a specified cardinal asks for a small part A of the objects of M generating S as a closed subcategory. Its expression as a union is followed by the explanation of the individual pieces. The accessibility and L-stability conditions on T continue at the head of 579.

**579 · Corollary 4.16.7.10.** The author equates three existence statements for an accessible M, concerning a nonaccessible closed subcategory, a nonaccessible open subcategory and a transfinite sequence of objects with vanishing forward Hom sets. He refers to the preceding corollary and 4.16.7.4. The margin supplies an example with k-algebras and specifies a universe.

**579–581 · Lemma 4.16.7.11.** For a full subcategory the author introduces a fully faithful functor from Indπ(S(π)) to M. Part a) describes its essential image using cofinality over x. Part b) uses that description to recognize π-accessibility. The proof passes from a presentation of x to a cofinal functor into Mπ/x, then uses the full inclusion. Conversely, a cofinality hypothesis changes the category indexing the displayed limit.

**581 · Lemma 4.16.7.12.** For a filtered I with complementary J closed and K open, the diagram relates “J cofinal”, “K non cofinal”, J≠∅ and K≠I by three equivalences. The proof given on the sheet is “Démonstration immédiate.”

**581–582 · Proof of 4.16.7.8.** The two lemmas are applied to the categories over x. The annotated chain moves from S to T by negating membership and cofinality, then interpreting each negation using the complement. The next paragraph relates nonemptiness over x to closed generation. A three-line attempt for T is struck. The live final sentence refers to the earlier stability formulation.

**583–584 · Section and cover.** The heading 4.17 returns to paratopos and names two operations, a boxed product and an underlined Hom with a lower exclamation mark. The next sheet carries XVIII and the accessible-categories title. No development of 4.17 follows on that face.

**585 · Working outline on a printed form.** The outline includes questions about operations on derivators, factorization, special parts, stability for Quillen structures, localizers of Cat, functors with infinity and W decorations, and external Hom. Crosses, changes of numbering and a cancelled “Catégories et Topos” belong to the plan. The printed letterhead has no completed date or addressee.

**586 · Cancelled calculation.** The author considers a surjectivity requirement for a map to a fibre product formed using F and G. A pair of arrows and classes of maps accompanies it. He asks for a containment involving the hatted product of W and W′. The lower calculations compare boxed products with underlined and ordinary Hom expressions. A single diagonal crosses the entire draft.

**587 · Two outlines.** The first runs from accessible categories and functors to accessible parts, open and closed subcategories, paratopos and operations on them. The second starts anew with factorization, a conjecture heading about the indicated parts, and stability for special Quillen structures. The object of “Conjectures sur” is one of the least secure words on the sheet.

## Statements left without proof

- **576.** “j’ai construit … un exemple” points to the appendix for the open subcategory. These sheets do not reproduce that construction.
- **577.** For 4.16.7.7 the manuscript calls the corollary “lui-même tautologique”. It gives the presentation and the equivalence, with no separate proof. The margin directs the reader to 4.16.7.8 for the pair of results.
- **579.** “Exemple où ces conditions sont satisfaites” introduces the marginal k-algebra case. The margin specifies k and the universe. It gives no indexed family of algebras or proof of the example here.
- **581.** The four-node diagram is followed by “Démonstration immédiate.” There are no further proof lines for this lemma.
- **585 and 587.** “Théorèmes de factorisation” and “Théorèmes de stabilité pour structures de Quillen” serve as outline headings; neither sheet sets out hypotheses or a proof for those planned theorems.

## Questions and conjectures

- **575–576.** “Je n’ai pas été capable de construire une suite … ni de prouver qu’une telle suite n’existe pas”. The condition immediately preceding the remark is Hom(xα,xβ)=∅ for α<β. The note at the star on 575 reads “Mais si finalement, cf 4.16.7.10 plus bas”.
- **576.** The question asks whether an L-stable subcategory “est tjrs accessible dans M”. The text considers both possibilities. “C’est faux cf plus bas” is a marginal response. The precise scope of this short response is best read beside the whole question.
- **585.** “Perplexités !” and “le pb d’existence” stand by the crossed operations on u. The placement of the handwritten note about extension to topos connects it to this part of the outline.
- **586.** “il faudrait que ce soit contenu dans” the hatted product of W and W′ ends with “est-ce raisonnable ?”. The author cancelled the draft containing the question.
- **587.** “Question pas clarifiée (question d’univers)”, “Questions ouvertes”, and “Conjectures sur … des dites parties” mark three different places. In the last heading the frozen first reading is *caractérisation*, with *cogénération* as an alternative. The sheet gives no conjecture precise enough to test.

## Slips

| Scan and line | Frozen wording | Possible intended form and grounds |
|---|---|---|
| 574, foot; 575, opening | 1) followed by b) | The proof calls the conditions a) and b). The first label appears as 1). This may be a numbering inconsistency. |
| 574, lines 13–15 | sα is called the first element outside the earlier subcategory | The selection of the first excluded element on 573 names xα. Replacing sα with xα would repeat that choice. The distinct letter is retained. |
| 578, last four lines | The union is indexed by ξ; the explanation then uses a as the left subscript of M | ξ would give the same bound letter as the union and the subsequent Hom. |
| 580, lines 15–17 | “l’image essentielle de S” | Part a) names the functor φ. Its essential image is the local referent; this may be an abbreviated reference to the induced functor. |
| 580, lines 18–21 | Indπ(M) | Indπ(Mπ) would be consistent with the category of objects over x in the same sentence. A missing subscript is a tentative interpretation. |
| 582, opening | The subcategory over x is called closed “de S(π)” | The displayed comparison uses Mπ/x as ambient category. That name would align the sentence with the diagram. |
| 582, last sentence | 4.6.7.6 | The corresponding proposition is headed 4.16.7.6 on 577. The shortened reference is clear on the crop; the mark following it is less certain. |

The endings after “d’une” on 576 and after “ou” on 587 are reading questions. The handwriting is too slight to attribute an error of agreement.

## Remarks of the model

- **M1 · High confidence.** The lower two conditions of the diagram on 581 agree already at the level of objects. Taking K to be the complementary full subcategory makes J≠∅ equivalent to K≠I. This checks just the bottom pair; it requires no reading of an overwritten sign.
- **M2 · High confidence.** For a complementary pair to which 4.16.7.9 applies, equivalence of the two accessibility predicates also gives equivalence of their negations. This accounts for the logical step behind the appeal to the preceding corollary on 579. The check is on negation of equivalent predicates and does not establish the categorical premise.
- **M3 · Low confidence.** The formula among the cancelled working on 586 may be related to the operation named in 4.17 on 583. Both sheets show a boxed product and Hom with a lower exclamation mark. The draft is struck and it gives no explicit cross-reference.
